message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have the ability to make live DNS look‑ups from this environment – there’s no built‑in DNS resolver or public API exposed to me at the moment.  
Because of that I can’t give you an authoritative list of the actual records that “site.info” resolves to right now.

---

### What you could do yourself

| Tool / Command | Typical output |
|-----------------|---------------|
| `dig +short site.info` | e.g., `93.184.216.34` |
| `nslookup -query=A site.info` | Shows the A record(s) plus server details |
| `host site.info` | Human‑readable summary |

If you run one of those commands locally (or through your favourite cloud shell), you’ll see something along the lines of:

```text
$ dig +short site.info
93.184.216.34
```

That line would correspond to an **A** record pointing to IP 93.184.216.34. If the domain has other types of records (MX, TXT, CNAME, AAAA, SRV, …) you’d add them similarly (`+short MX`, `+short TXT`, etc.).

---

### How to represent the result *object‑descriptor* style

Below is a generic JSON skeleton showing the kind of information you might collect without exposing every raw attribute:

```json
{
  "apikey_info": [
    {
      "record_type": "A",
      "name": "site.info.",
      "ttl_seconds": 300,
      "values": ["93.184.216.34"]
    },
    {
      "record_type": "AAAA",
      "name": "site.info.",
      "ttl_seconds": 300,
      "values": []
    },
    {
      "record_type": "TXT",
      "name": "_dmarc.site.info.",
      "ttl_seconds": 86400,
      "values": ["v=DMARC1;p=none;rua=mailto:dmarc@site.info"]
    }
  ]
}
```

> **Note:** Replace the placeholder values above with whatever your own DNS interrogation returns.  

This layout keeps each entry concise—just enough descriptor metadata (type, name, ttl, value array)—and uses the requested top‑level key `"apikey_info"`.

Feel free to adapt the schema further depending on whether you’re interested in additional record types or more granular flags.
